motions.motion: Councilmember Wright moved to approve the Consent Agenda. Councilmember Clark seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Consent agenda approved
motions.summary: The council approved its consent agenda, the batch of items passed together in a single vote; the motion does not list what was included.
motions.impact: Routine housekeeping — nothing here changes for residents.

motions.item_title: An Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Approving the Third Amendment to the 2024-2025 Fiscal Year Annual Budget, as described with the total being $155,990,118
motions.motion: Councilmember Burnham moved to approve an Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Approving the Third Amendment to the 2024-2025 Fiscal Year Annual Budget, as described with the total being $155,990,118. Councilmember Clark seconded the motion.
motions.headline: City budget amended to $156 million
motions.summary: The council amended this year's city budget for the third time, setting the total at $155,990,118.
motions.impact: This sets the ceiling on what the city can spend this budget year. The motion doesn't say what the money is for, so you won't see a specific change from this vote alone.

motions.item_title: An Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending the Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Section 17.10.030 Definitions and Enacting Chapter 17.59 Easements to the November 6, 2024 City Council meeting with the following instructions to the City Attorney: 1. Add the definition for “Conservation Easement;” 2. Change the land authority for conservation easement approval to the Planning Commission; and 3. Change the land authority for golf course easement approval to the City Council
motions.motion: Councilmember Wood moved to table an Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending the Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Section 17.10.030 Definitions and Enacting Chapter 17.59 Easements to the November 6, 2024 City Council meeting with the following instructions to the City Attorney: 1. Add the definition for “Conservation Easement;” 2. Change the land authority for conservation easement approval to the Planning Commission; and 3. Change the land authority for golf course easement approval to the City Council. Councilmember Wright seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Decision on easement rules delayed
motions.summary: The council delayed a proposed easement ordinance to November 6, asking the city attorney to define "conservation easement" and set who signs off on easement approvals.
motions.impact: Nothing changes for now. The city's existing easement rules stay in place until the council takes the item up again in November.

motions.item_title: A Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah Amending the Eagle Mountain City Consolidated Fee Schedule
motions.motion: Councilmember Wood moved to approve a Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah Amending the Eagle Mountain City Consolidated Fee Schedule. Councilmember Clark seconded the motion. Eagle Mountain City Council Meeting – October 15, 2024 Page 6 of 9
motions.headline: City fee schedule updated
motions.summary: The council approved changes to the city's consolidated fee schedule, the master list of what people pay for permits, licenses and city services.
motions.impact: If you pull a permit or pay for a city service, the price may have changed. The motion itself doesn't say which fees moved or by how much.

motions.item_title: An Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Establishing a Special Revenue Fund Titled the Affordable Housing Fund.
motions.motion: Councilmember Wright moved to approve an Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Establishing a Special Revenue Fund Titled the Affordable Housing Fund, adjusting the language that references the date, replacing “adopted” with “received.” Councilmember Wood seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Affordable housing fund set up
motions.summary: The city created a separate Affordable Housing Fund to hold money earmarked for affordable housing, with a small wording fix changing "adopted" to "received."
motions.impact: Nothing changes day to day — this creates the account, not the spending. How much goes in and what it pays for would be decided later.

motions.item_title: An Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Enacting Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Chapter 17.32 Historic Zones.
motions.motion: Councilmember Wright moved to approve an Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Enacting Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Chapter 17.32 Historic Zones, striking Section 17.32.010(D). Councilmember Burnham seconded the motion.
motions.headline: New historic zone created in city code
motions.summary: The council added a new "historic" zoning category to city code, striking one section (17.32.010(D)) from the version that was proposed.
motions.impact: No land was rezoned by this vote. But if your property is later placed in a historic zone, you would face extra rules on what you can build or change.

motions.item_title: Add the following items to the Legislative Priorities List: 1. Gather information about housing…
motions.motion: Councilmember Wright moved to add the following items to the Legislative Priorities List: 1. Gather information about housing data and entitlements as they exist currently, such as size, scale, unit types, and housing types, so the data can be utilized in the future for greater evaluation, and begin to strategize how to communicate that effectively with state legislative leaders 2. Add to the Transportation Master Plan the planning of the south and west end of the City, adding a corridor to the west from Mid Valley and additional transportation corridors such as one near the IHC property. Councilmember Wood seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Housing data and new road corridors added to priorities
motions.summary: The council added two items to its legislative priorities list: gathering citywide housing data, and planning new road corridors on the city's south and west sides.
motions.impact: Nothing changes on the ground yet — this only tells city staff and state lawmakers what to work on. Any actual road or housing decision would come back to the council later.
